name: Mary Candle

attributes.attribute: a wax candle melted and rubbed into a cow's hide as a milking charm
used to protect the milk supply from theft by witches and fairies
most vital at Beltane, on May 1, when witches and fairies tried to steal milk
folkloric rituals meant to guard the cows' milk supply

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: A Mary Candle was a wax candle used in the milking charms of the Celtic lands. The candle was melted and the wax was rubbed into a cow's hide. The rite protected the animal's milk from theft by witches and fairies. It was most needed around Beltane, the feast of summer's beginning on May 1, when fairies roved about trying to steal the milk from the cows' udders. Alongside the Mary Candle, twigs of rowan were tied to the cows' tails.
